title: 1 m 18 AWG test lead with crocodile clips

sources.citation: International Annealed Copper Standard (adopted by the IEC in 1913, published as IEC 60028, whose 1925 edition is a revision): annealed copper has a resistivity of 1/58 Ω·mm²/m (1.7241 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m) at 20 °C (293.15 K), and a temperature coefficient of resistance of 0.00393 per kelvin at 20 °C. The lead's resistance is computed from these (resistivity × length ÷ area, with the temperature coefficient), never taken from a conductor table.

18 AWG, the usual gauge of US bench test leads (NEC/US-first). The area is derived from the public AWG definition (ASTM B258): d = 0.127 mm × 92^((36 − n)/39), so 18 AWG is d ≈ 1.0237 mm and A = π d²/4 ≈ 0.8231 mm² (8.2305e-7 m²); it is not taken from any NEC table. Stranding is ignored: real flexible leads measure about 10 % above this solid-wire figure.
game-design: a 1 m bench test lead, a common retail length.

10 mΩ at each end, where a sprung test clip grips a terminal: typical published test-clip contact ratings are roughly 6 to 15 mΩ (paraphrased from manufacturers' clip specifications; no single vendor).

The lead's copper, as the materials table's annealed-copper row cites it (F3.6 part 1, ADR 0018 §8): NBS Handbook 100, Copper Wire Tables (1966, read in full by electrical-realism-reviewer), a density of 8.89 g/cm³ and resistance linear in temperature up to 200 °C (473.15 K), where the engine clamps R(T); a specific heat of 385 J/(kg·K) near 25 °C from the NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables (Chase, 4th ed., 1998) through the NIST Chemistry WebBook's Shomate fit (24.47 J/(mol·K) ÷ 63.546 g/mol). Paraphrased; no table reproduced.

The lead's PVC insulation, as the insulation table cites it (ADR 0018 §8): a thermal conductivity of 0.18 W/(m·K), mid-band of PVC's 0.16 to 0.20 W/(m·K) from a plastics distributor's published thermal-property table (read by electrical-realism-reviewer in the P3 source pre-audit), and the table's game-design surface emissivity of 0.9 (an infrared-thermometer maker's table gives about 0.93 for PVC). Paraphrased.

game-design, anchored to the 600 V PVC hookup-wire wall, about 0.8 mm for 18 AWG in manufacturers' public sheets (no single maker): one PVC layer; the lead's thermal model takes the conductor solid-round at its nominal area.
